extracted.intended_audience: machine learning / IR researchers and engineers working on paper–reviewer matching and academic recommendation systems
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, pre-training, and evaluating models that match academic submissions to reviewers (paper–reviewer relevance). Covers dataset construction, pre-training objectives for semantic/topic/citation factors, model architecture (instruction- and paper-encoders), negative sampling, and evaluation metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance rating scale (0–3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotations use a four-level relevance score: “3” (very relevant), “2” (relevant), “1” (slightly relevant), or “0” (irrelevant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the ground-truth label for paper–reviewer pairs in multiple datasets (NIPS, SciRepEval, KDD). The scale is the basis for Soft/Hard settings and metric computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soft vs Hard relevance settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Soft setting: reviewers with a score of “2” or “3” are considered relevant; Hard setting: only reviewers with a score of “3” are viewed as relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines binary relevance for evaluation. Different experiments report results under both settings to capture permissive vs strict relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision at K (P@K) evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt P@5 and P@10 as evaluation metrics: Soft P@K = average over papers of (# top-K ranked reviewers with score >= 2) / K; Hard P@K = average over papers of (# top-K ranked reviewers with score == 3) / K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow prior work (Mimno and McCallum; Singh et al.). Use these metrics to compare ranking performance across methods and datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset diversity and annotation procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation should use multiple public datasets across domains (e.g., NIPS, SciRepEval, SIGIR, KDD) with documented numbers of papers, reviewers, and annotated (p,r) pairs and annotation procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIPS: 34 papers, 190 reviewers, 393 annotated pairs by 9 researchers. SciRepEval: combines multiple sources. SIGIR: aspect-based annotations mapped to 0–3 via discretized Jaccard similarity. KDD: newly annotated (174 papers, 737 reviewers) by 5 data mining researchers. Use such diversity to test generality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of factor-specific pre-training data
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-train instruction-guided paper encoder separately for each factor using appropriate data: Search dataset for semantic factor, MAPLE benchmark for topic factor, and citation triplets for citation factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each factor has a distinct pretraining objective aligned to the notion of relevance for that factor (semantic: query–document clicks; topic: shared fine-grained research fields; citation: citing relationships). See Appendix A.1.1 for more data details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor-specific semantic objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: For the semantic factor, treat submission p as a query and reviewer-profile paper q as a document; learn g(·|ϕ) to maximize the inner product between ad-hoc query and semantically relevant document in vector space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses Search dataset (queries from an academic search engine and click-through derived relevant documents) to form positive pairs for contrastive pre-training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor-specific topic objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: For the topic factor, train g(·|ϕ) to maximize inner product for two papers p and q if they share common research fields (derived from MAPLE with fine-grained fields-of-study).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct topically relevant paper pairs using Microsoft Academic Graph tags; MAPLE provides millions of papers with fine-grained field tags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor-specific citation objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: For the citation factor, train g(·|ϕ) to maximize inner product for two papers p and q if p cites q, leveraging large collections of citation triplets (p, q+, q−).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow prior work (Cohan et al., Ostendorff et al.) to form positive and negative examples for contrastive pretraining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrastive pre-training objective (infoNCE-style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use contrastive loss J = -log( exp(g(p|ϕ)ᵀ g(q+|ϕ)) / (exp(g(p|ϕ)ᵀ g(q+|ϕ)) + Σ_t exp(g(p|ϕ)ᵀ g(q_t^-|ϕ))) ) to train Enc_i(·) and Enc_p(·) jointly across factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimize sum_ϕ sum_{(p,q^+,q^-_1,...,q^-_T)} J. Samples include one positive q+ and multiple negatives q^-_t.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction sampling per training sample
rubrics_metrics.description: For each pre-training sample (p, q+, q^-_1,...,q^-_T), randomly pick an instruction i_ϕ corresponding to factor ϕ, and encode it with the instruction encoder Enc_i(·) to obtain g(·|ϕ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This makes the encoder produce factor-conditioned representations; instructions are used as contexts during paper encoding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard negative mining strategy (factor-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine in-batch negatives as easy negatives with factor-specific hard negative selection rules: semantic hard negatives are shown but not clicked given query p; topic hard negatives share venue but no fine-grained field with p; citation hard negatives are papers cited by q+ but not cited by p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following Cohan et al., such hard negatives boost contrastive learning performance. Implement both in-batch easy negatives (Karpukhin et al.) and the described factor-aware hard negatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared encoder parameters across factors
rubrics_metrics.description: The parameters of the instruction encoder Enc_i(·) and the paper encoder Enc_p(·) are shared during training across different factor instances and across the three factors, so the model carries common knowledge from pretraining data of different factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sharing allows parameter efficiency and cross-factor transfer while instruction tokens provide factor specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asymmetric MHA instruction-guided encoding
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an asymmetric multi-head attention (MHA_asy) where the paper encoder's MHA attends to the concatenation [H_{i_ϕ}^{(l)} ∥ H_p^{(l)}], i.e., instruction representations serve as context for paper encoding, but the paper does not serve as context for instruction encoding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formally: MHA_asy(H_p^{(l)}, ẼH_p^{(l)}) uses ẼH_p^{(l)} = H_{i_ϕ}^{(l)} ∥ H_p^{(l)} in the attention keys/values. This design keeps instruction semantics stable and makes final paper representation aware of factor ϕ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encoder architecture and final representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Both Enc_i(·) and Enc_p(·) have 12 Transformer layers; the final instruction-guided representation of paper p is the output embedding of its [CLS] token after the last layer: g(p|ϕ) = h_[CLS]^{(12)}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Transformer layer operations with LayerNorm, (asymmetric) MHA, and FFN as described in Eqs. (6)–(9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation: mapping aspect-level annotations to ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: For datasets like SIGIR where papers/reviewers are assigned aspect tags, compute Jaccard similarity between a paper's aspects and a reviewer's aspects and discretize it to map to the 0–3 rating scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns aspect-based datasets with the 0–3 rating convention used across datasets for comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical significance reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report when CoF is significantly better than baselines with p-value thresholds: * for p < 0.05 and ** for p < 0.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use significance markers in tables to indicate methods that are statistically outperformed; bold the highest score.
